subject: Tenant comms: hardened topology and cross-tenant communication matrix (RFP follow-up)
messages:
From: Aurora Bank Security Team <security@aurorabank.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: RFP follow-up: hardened tenant communication topology

Hi Markus,

Thanks for your initial RFP submission. A couple of follow-ups from our architecture review team: we need a concise topology diagram that highlights allowed tenant-facing and internal control-plane communication paths, specifically:

- Cross-tenant traffic controls and any default-deny behavior between runtime containers/pods
- How KV cache fetches and sidecar proxies are isolated from other tenants
- Egress controls for log/metrics collectors and whether there are shared collectors across tenants

Can you provide: (1) a PNG or draw.io export of the topology with annotated communication lanes, (2) a spreadsheet mapping each service to allowed outbound destinations and ports, and (3) a short threat model summary (one page) that enumerates the top 3 attack vectors and compensating controls?

We'd like this by EOD Wednesday (2026-12-22) so we can include it in our procurement packet. Also point us to any compliance artifacts (SOC2 snapshot, network segregation evidence).

Thanks,
Priya Reddy
Security Architect, Aurora Bank
priya.reddy@aurorabank.com

--
Aurora Bank | Information Security

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@aurorabank.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 11:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: hardened tenant communication topology

Priya —

Thanks for the clear ask. Attaching an annotated PNG and a comms matrix workbook that map services -> allowed egress/ports. Quick highlights below while your team reviews the artifacts:

- Default-deny: All tenant compute runs in per-tenant VPC segments with enforced network policies; inter-tenant routing is blocked at the uplink and by an application-level allowlist.
- KV cache isolation: KV cache instances are namespace-scoped; read-through caches use short-lived credentials and per-request token binding; cross-tenant keys are never colocated with tenant KV shards.
- Sidecar vs dedicated proxy: We support both sidecar proxying and dedicated tenant proxies. In hosted mode we default to per-tenant dedicated proxies to minimize shared mid-tier state.
- Egress: Telemetry and logs are sent to per-tenant collectors by default (centralized retention is opt-in). All outbound flows are whitelisted by destination FQDN/IP ranges; metadata endpoints are blocked from tenant compute unless explicitly allowed for managed updates.

Attachments: redwood_hardened_topology_v1.png, comms-path-matrix.xlsx
Also added a 1-page threat-summary in the topology slide notes (see PNG).

Next steps: if you want, we can join a 30-minute technical deep-dive on Wednesday morning.

Best,
Markus Klein
Principal Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai

Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 12:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: hardened tenant communication topology

Priya / team —

Thank you for the review. A couple technical clarifications that I added to the comms matrix:

- Lateral traffic: Pod-to-pod (or container-to-container) is restricted via RBAC + network policy. We enforce policy at the hypervisor/network agent level so even if a tenant gets code execution, arbitrary port-scanning across tenants is mitigated.
- KV cache egress: For customers with strict egress rules we offer an option to pin KV instances to the customer's VPC with NAT gateways managed by Aurora-style allowlists (customer-provisioned).
- Control plane demarcation: Control plane (provisioning, telemetry piping) uses a separate management network with explicit ACLs; runtime tokens are scoped and short-lived — no long-lived control-plane keys are embedded in runtime images.

I've attached a draw.io flow (kv-cache-egress-flow.drawio) that shows the recommended patterns for high-security customers. Karthik — could you include the annotated port table before Wednesday?

-Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Product Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai

From: Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@aurorabank.com>

Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 21 Dec 2026 09:21:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: hardened tenant communication topology

Markus / Vanessa —

Appreciate the materials. A few follow-ups from our network team after a quick pass:

1) Can you confirm whether control-plane observers (tracing/metrics collectors) ever accept inbound push from tenant compute, or is it strictly pull from a managed collector? Which ports/protocols are used for telemetry?

2) On KV isolation: your note about "short-lived credentials" — please capture the issuance flow and revocation triggers (e.g., on redeploy or node termination). We need to understand token lifetime and rotation cadence.

3) Compliance artifacts: can you provide a redacted SOC2 snapshot and any network segmentation evidence (we will accept logs showing tenant-to-collector IP mappings for a 48-hour window)?

Finally, we'd like to schedule the deep-dive — how does Wednesday 10:00 AM PT look for a 30-minute session?

Thanks,
Priya Reddy
Security Architect, Aurora Bank

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@aurorabank.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 22 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: hardened tenant communication topology

Priya —

Thanks — confirmed on the proposed time, we are booked for Wednesday 10:00 AM PT (calendar invite sent). Quick answers and links below so your network/compliance teams have something to ingest ahead of the call: 

- Telemetry model: by default telemetry is PUSH from tenant runtime to a per-tenant collector endpoint over TLS 1.3 (mutual TLS available). Ports: 443 for HTTPS push; optional gRPC telemetry on 4317 when enabled. Pull-only mode is available for air-gapped/private deployments.

- Token lifecycle: short-lived signed tokens (JWTs) issued by the control-plane token service with a 5-minute TTL by default; revocation occurs on redeploy, manual revoke from the console, or when the node instance terminates (control-plane publishes a revocation event that immediately rejects new tokens). We can provide a sequence diagram on the call.

- Compliance artifacts: attached SOC2-snapshot-2026.pdf. For segmentation evidence we can provide a redacted 48-hour flow log export — karthik and Neha will prepare and upload to the drive link by EOD tomorrow.

Action items (assigned):
- Karthik Iyer: produce annotated port table and redacted flow logs (attachments/upload).
- Neha Kapoor: prepare redacted SOC2 support note and evidence bundle.
- Vanessa: be ready to cover KV cache isolation patterns on the call.

We will use the Drive link (https://drive.redwood.example.com/open?id=1a2b3c-topology-review) for evidence exchange; DocuSign link is for the NDA amendment if needed.

Looking forward to the call.

Best,
Markus
Principal Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
